paper.title_en: Optimal Impure $(r,δ)$-Quantum Locally Recoverable Codes with Explicit Minimum Localities
paper.abstract_en: Quantum locally recoverable codes with $(r,δ)$-locality ($(r,δ)$-qLRCs) are quantum error-correcting codes in which $δ-1$ erased qudits can be recovered by accessing only $r$ other qudits. The minimum locality of a qLRC is the least $r$ such that it has $(r,δ)$-locality. This paper aims to construct optimal impure $(r,δ)$-qLRCs with disjoint recovering sets and explicit minimum localities, where the optimality is measured by the Singleton-like bound of Guruswami, Kshirsagar, and Trivedi (GKT-optimal). Such qLRCs have particular advantages in recovering as many quantum erasures as possible while operating in parallel and with minimal qudit access overhead. We first characterize the recovering sets and the minimum locality of any CSS code by local relative distances, which are relative minimum distances of punctured codes with respect to shortened codes. We then construct impure qLRCs as CSS codes from nested pairs of generalized monomial-Cartesian codes. Grouping the monomials by their degree in the last variable, we reduce both their minimum distances and their local recovery to nested pairs of codes in the remaining variables, and the coordinates with the same values of these variables form disjoint recovering sets. In this way, we obtain four infinite families of GKT-optimal impure $(r,δ)$-qLRCs with disjoint recovering sets, and determine their minimum localities and the recovering sets attaining them for every admissible $δ$, except for a partial range of $δ$ in one family. These minimum localities need not be monotone in $δ$. In particular, two of the families contain GKT-optimal impure subfamilies of CSS codes CSS$(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C})$ with $(r,δ)$-locality for some $r<n-δ+1$ at values of $δ$ for which $\mathcal{C}$ has no classical $(r',δ)$-locality for any $0<r'<n$, where $n$ is the length of $\mathcal{C}$.
